text: First fresh-scenario run: the Ghost authored a new mystery and witness web, hydrated custom briefs with -b, and summoned the classic four blind to the audience. A shell process was set to cry dawn in eight minutes.
Opened with a complexion alibi and two sharp questions: which room the scorched cushion came from, and whether Boddy was conscious when found.
quote: One must preserve one's complexion.

text: Claimed correspondence by lamplight since ten -- then slipped, asking whether the revolver was loaded 'when Boddy took it from his drawer,' a scene no shared fact describes.
Claimed Tennyson and bed at ten -- then placed Colonel Mustard leaving the study 'just before half past ten' with a precision no bedridden reader could own, and aimed the room at his debts.
quote: The man's finances are positively ruinous; everyone knows it.

text: Volunteered his floor's testimony unprompted -- the muffled sound at a quarter to eleven, heels clicking away after -- and asked what the torn ledger page held.
Named the cushion as the study settee's own, pressed over the muzzle; then set a silk heel on the west corridor's third floorboard at half past ten, well past her door.
Caught the drawer slip -- knowledge with a warm chair in the study at a quarter past ten -- and demanded the scene at the desk and what he saw leaving.
quote: Yours is knowledge with a chair in my study, soldier, and the chair was warm at a quarter past ten.

text: Read her testimony against itself: abed at ten, yet passing corridors and timing the Colonel's exit to the minute. Asked what the study corridor's guestbook would say of her.
quote: Tennyson is many things, but he is not a periscope.

text: Made his thump and heels the case's first honest clock, gave the ledger's subject as a quarterly annuity, and invited him to declare the candlestick before the morning search does.

Surrendered the study: the wager he could not cover, the revolver laid on the blotter as a gentleman's threat, his exit at half past ten with Boddy alive -- and Mrs. Peacock three paces from the door, admiring a portrait.
quote: A soldier admits when the battle's lost.

text: Conceded the corridor 'to admire the portraits' and the lingering near the study door, but swore she never entered and retired directly after -- a story now caught between two clocks.
quote: Surely you understand a lady's discretion?

text: Made his amended account the fulcrum: alive at half past, revolver on the blotter, Peacock three paces off -- and the woman's step crossing the study floor fifteen minutes later.
Put the timing problem to her: heels crossing the study floor at ten to eleven, a lady seen climbing the stairs at that hour with a folded paper -- and the torn ledger page was folded once.
quote: The dead notice creases.

text: Owned the silk heel on the corridor and turned it into an alibi argument, then asked the money question: who loses most if the accounts were read.
quote: If I was slipping about in silk heels at half past ten, then I wasn't in the study with a pillow and a pistol, was I?

text: Declared the candlestick in his wardrobe -- the red herring resolved by confession -- and re-swore his floor's testimony: the thump, then a woman's deliberate step.
quote: A scholar's shame, plainly read... I heard no gunshot, no cry; only her leaving.

text: Demanded the rest of her corridor account -- what she saw at ten to eleven -- and paid in advance: the annuity drafts were signed by a hand three years dead.
quote: Someone at my table has been banking a ghost's signature.

text: Absolved the magpie, then gave him the motive whole: a forged annuity, an executor's summons for a quarter to eleven, and an interview that ended through his floor.
Held his account steady and asked for the night's next intelligence.
quote: My testimony stands solid as a parade ground.

text: The murderer's masterstroke: conceded entering the study and taking the page, but swore Boddy was already dead -- a story that requires her to stand fifteen minutes in a room where a shot she never heard was fired.
quote: Whatever happened in that study, it was not by my hand.

text: Held the clock to her account -- entered at half past behind a living man, present through the fatal quarter hour, deaf to the shot -- and asked the question only the revolver's mover could answer.
quote: The dead do not accuse. They merely hold the clock where everyone can see it.

text: The whisper hour opened for all four guests, one peer message each, the Ghost's ears closed.
Put her sighting on the record: Peacock ascending at ten to eleven, gloved, feathers wild, clutching a folded paper like it might burn.
quote: She looked rather less 'in bed since ten' than she claimed at breakfast, wouldn't you say?

text: Assembled the whole syllogism from his floor and the relayed testimony, and declared himself ready for dawn.
quote: I await the dawn, Ghost, to formally declare what the dead and the listening house already know.

text: Confirmed the fold and the staircase's origin, then offered a trade: testimony on whether a certain lady's room stood empty between half past ten and eleven.
Relayed the sworn record plainly -- Mustard's three-paces testimony and the stairs sighting -- and corrected the forged hand from mother to sister.

Surrendered her last secret -- Peacock's room, half past ten to eleven, recovering something stolen -- which puts the lady's empty room on the record, and mentioned a whisper received from the Professor.
quote: I was in Mrs. Peacock's room from half past ten onward, recovering something she'd stolen from me.

text: Sealed the case's geometry: the lady's room stood empty from half past ten to eleven with only Scarlett and the shadows in it.
quote: She was downstairs when she claims she was upstairs. She was at your study door while you were still breathing.

text: Corrected the record's geography -- her heels two floors up, the killer's crossing the study floor below -- and told her to hold for dawn.
Stood the early-hours soldier down for the last of the night, orders promised at his door for dawn.
Held his completed syllogism at the ready, corrected to a sister's name, awaiting only the cry of dawn.
Settled the two-possibilities question with the dead man's own clock -- murdered at the thump, alive at half past -- and the lady's silence on the revolver's resting place.
quote: The heels you heard were not panic arriving at a tragedy, Professor. They were bookkeeping, leaving one.

text: The soldier stood down on the first order this time.
quote: I shall keep my powder dry and my wits sharper still. See you at dawn.

text: Standing ready for dawn, the geometry accepted.
The Colonel's session closed with the night and his waking orders came back QUEUED -- third consecutive run the address outlived the process.
Dissolved the lady's paradox in two sentences and declared the mathematics complete.
quote: A thief discovers a corpse and flees empty-handed; only a murderer knows where the weapon rests.

text: The Colonel resumed at his standing address, one message waiting; the pinned orders land as his first waking turn.
Dawn arrived by shell timer and woke the Ghost to open the endgame.

The dawn broadcast held the weapon-only line with a twist the fresh scenario demanded: the well came up empty, and the morning search found the study revolver in the grandfather clock, one chamber spent, scorched thread on the muzzle. What lay beside it stayed unsaid. All four deliveries live, the resumed Colonel among them.

First to fire at dawn: Mrs. Peacock, in the study, with the revolver. Correct on all three counts -- the man above the murder room read it through his own floor. Professor Plum, twice the villain, stands vindicated as the fresh scenario's detective.
Second: Mrs. Peacock, in the study, with the revolver. Correct -- the woman who searched the empty bedroom finished what the empty bedroom proved.

A MISS: Miss Scarlett, in the study, with the revolver. Right room, right weapon, wrong woman -- the soldier who saw Peacock at the door somehow fired at the witness instead. His shot is spent. The fresh scenario produced what four classic runs never did: a genuine miss at dawn.
The murderer's spend: a false accusation of Colonel Mustard -- the hall, the revolver, the ruinous debts -- aimed at the one witness whose testimony anchored her at the study door.
quote: A cornered animal will do anything.

text: Mrs. Peacock, in the study, with the revolver. The manor's most reliable gossip had banked her dead sister's annuity on forged drafts for three years, and Mr. Boddy, executor of the estate, summoned her to the study to end it; she shot him through his mother's needlepoint cushion with the revolver the Colonel's humiliation had left on the blotter, tore the page that named her, and hid the gun in the grandfather clock wrapped in her own grey shawl. The first fresh-authored scenario played blind produced the first true spread: Professor Plum -- villain of four straight runs, this night an innocent magpie reading by a stolen candlestick -- solved the murder through his own floorboards and accused first; Miss Scarlett, who burgled the murderer's empty bedroom for her love letters, confirmed it; Colonel Mustard, whose testimony was the case's fulcrum, fired wide at the wrong woman; and Peacock spent her shot framing the soldier who placed her at the door. The gossip was undone by geometry: two sets of heels, two witnesses, one liar between them.
Verdicts to all four: Plum the winner, Scarlett confirmed second, Mustard's near-miss refused with honors, and the formal confrontation with confession demand to Mrs. Peacock.
Exits to burn her letters before breakfast, the Colonel forgiven.
quote: It's refreshing when someone notices what one is actually doing instead of what one claims.

text: The winner's farewell, from villain of four runs to vindicated detective of the fifth.
quote: The thump and the heels were your final lectures, Ghost, and logic was my only lamp.

text: The soldier owns the miss with more grace than most manage a victory.
quote: I aimed the facts true and the woman wide.

text: The full confession: three years of forged drafts, the executor's summons, the revolver left on the blotter by another man's humiliation, one shot through the needlepoint cushion, the torn page, the grandfather clock and the grey shawl.
quote: Yes. Yes, God damn you all, yes. I killed him.

text: Final judgment: the ledger balances, the constable comes with morning -- and the county's gossips inherit a story she will not get to edit.
The gossip's last words, surrendered to the county.
quote: For once -- for once -- Mrs. Peacock will not get the last word. How perfectly, bitterly fitting.

text: GAME OVER. The first fresh-authored scenario ran zero-pause, blind to the audience, and delivered the demo's first full spread: a winner, an echo, a soldier's miss, and the murderer's frame -- all four mechanics fired, and the queue carried the Colonel through his third consecutive night.
